title: ARK’s Expected Share Price For Tesla In 2031
gist: ARK's updated open-source Monte Carlo model puts Tesla's expected 2031 share price at ~$4,400 (bear ~$3,300, bull ~$5,000), on ~$1.45 trillion revenue and a 61% EBITDA margin. Robotaxi makes up ~80% of enterprise value (down from ~90% in the 2024 model) because Optimus Robot-as-a-Service is projected to reach ~1 million units and ~$200 billion in revenue. The model also assumes ~$225 billion of cumulative AI infrastructure spend tied to the Terafab project with SpaceX.

insights.claim: ARK's updated open-source Monte Carlo model for Tesla yields an expected value of ~$4,400 per share in 2031, with bull and bear cases (75th and 25th percentile outcomes) of ~$5,000 and ~$3,300, versus a 2025 actual share price of ~$450.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Implies ~62% price CAGR to 2031 in the base case; even ARK's bear case implies ~53% annualized returns, signaling how far its framing sits from consensus.
insights.quote: ARK’s updated open-source Tesla model yields an expected value of ~$4,400 per share in 2031.
insights.locator: ARK’s updated open-source Tesla model yields

insights.claim: ARK's model draws on distributions across 32 independent inputs, and it defines bull and bear not as discrete scenarios but as the 75th and 25th percentile outputs of the simulation.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: The narrow interquartile band ($3,300-$5,000) reflects input distributions chosen by ARK; the real tail risk (e.g., robotaxi failure) sits outside the published cases.
insights.quote: each case is defined as the 75th and 25th percentile output of the simulation

insights.claim: In ARK's base case, Tesla's 2031 total revenue reaches ~$1,449 billion (from $95 billion in 2025), EBITDA ~$902 billion, gross margin 68% and EBITDA margin 61%, supporting an enterprise value of ~$16.4 trillion and market cap of ~$17.5 trillion.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A ~15x revenue increase in six years with margins quadrupling from 15% is the core bet; any underwriting must stress-test the margin mix shift toward software-like robotaxi and RaaS revenue.

insights.claim: ARK's base case has ride-hail net revenue of ~$753 billion in 2031 from ~8.1 million robotaxi vehicles, making it the single largest revenue line, ahead of EV revenue (~$320 billion on 10.2 million cars sold) and Optimus (~$212 billion).
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Robotaxi economics dominate the valuation; car-sale volume (6x 2025's 1.6 million) is a secondary driver in ARK's construction.

insights.claim: ARK's base case projects Tesla energy storage deployments of ~2,278 GWh in 2031 versus 47 GWh in 2025, generating ~$163 billion of storage revenue.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A ~48x scale-up in storage is an under-discussed component of the model and would make Tesla a dominant grid-battery supplier if realized.

insights.claim: Despite a ~$17.5 trillion base-case market cap, ARK's model implies a 2031 cash flow yield of ~4.2%, up from ~0.5% in 2025.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: ARK argues the 2031 target is not a stretched multiple of 2031 cash flows; the risk is entirely in delivering the cash flows, not in terminal valuation.

insights.claim: ARK's 2031 target of ~$4,400 represents an increase from its prior 2024 model, which estimated an expected value of $2,600 per share in 2029.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: ARK has raised rather than tempered its target after robotaxi launched, signaling increasing conviction in the autonomy thesis.
insights.quote: ARK’s Expected Value For Tesla In 2029: $2,600 Per Share.

themes.theme: Robotaxi as the core of value

insights.claim: ARK estimates Robotaxi will account for ~80% of Tesla's enterprise value in 2031, down from ~90% in 2029 in its 2024 model, primarily because Optimus Robot-as-a-Service is expected to inflect as robotaxis proliferate.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Tesla in ARK's framing is overwhelmingly an autonomy-platform bet; the auto business is close to irrelevant to the valuation.
insights.quote: ARK estimates that Robotaxi will account for ~80% of Tesla’s enterprise value in 2031, down from ~90% in 2029

insights.claim: Tesla launched its robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025, has scaled to seven cities across three states, and completed more than 1 million unsupervised driverless miles in ~7 months, ~4x faster than Waymo's first million.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Early ramp velocity versus Waymo is ARK's evidence that Tesla's scaling curve is steeper, a key competitive datapoint in autonomous ride-hail.
insights.quote: has completed more than 1 million unsupervised driverless miles in ~7 months, ~4x faster than Waymo’s first million

insights.claim: Tesla has framed Full Self-Driving V15, expected late this year, as the gating factor for scaling its robotaxi service.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: FSD V15's release and performance is the near-term catalyst to watch for validation or delay of the robotaxi ramp.
insights.quote: Tesla has framed FSD V15 as the gating factor for scaling its robotaxi service.

insights.claim: ARK's research suggests that, at equal utilization, Tesla's operational cost per mile will be ~40% lower than Waymo's next-gen robotaxi, thanks to vertical integration and a vision-only approach, with the Cybercab now added to the fleet.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A structural cost advantage would let Tesla undercut rivals on price and win share in autonomous ride-hail; it is the moat claim underpinning the robotaxi EV.
insights.quote: at equal utilization rates, Tesla’s operational costs per mile will be ~40% lower than those for Waymo’s next-gen robotaxi

insights.claim: Tesla could scale robotaxi supply through consumer-owned vehicles, raising utilization and lowering operating costs further; ARK's base case has ~8 million robotaxis deployed cumulatively by 2031.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A capital-light fleet model using customer cars would let Tesla scale supply faster than fleet-owning competitors.
insights.quote: In our base case, Tesla deploys ~8 million robotaxis cumulatively by 2031.

insights.claim: ARK argues cheap, highly utilized robotaxis can operate profitably below today's ride-hail prices and thereby expand the ride-hail market well beyond today's human-driven market, which it now models with income-segmented willingness-to-pay.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: The TAM is assumed elastic to price; incumbents' current ride-hail volumes understate the addressable market in ARK's view.
insights.quote: autonomous robotaxis could expand the ride-hail market well beyond today’s human-driven market

insights.claim: ARK excludes dynamic pricing from its model to be conservative, although higher-income consumers travel disproportionately during congested periods, which could let a robotaxi network charge more at peak and cut prices off-peak to expand utilization.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Peak-pricing optionality is an unmodeled upside lever in ARK's robotaxi revenue.
insights.quote: Although dynamic pricing could add to the upside, we have excluded it from our model to be conservative.

insights.claim: ARK has removed Tesla's China robotaxi operations from its model, expecting Tesla to prioritize the US due to higher ride-hail pricing power and profit potential, and also dropped human-driven ride-hail and insurance with de minimis price-target impact.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: China is treated as zero in the autonomy valuation, a notable concession on geographic scope.
insights.quote: we have removed its China Robotaxi operations from our model

insights.claim: ARK says humanoid robots could scale to a ~$26 trillion total addressable market, roughly twice the robotaxi TAM of $10-15 trillion, corroborating Elon Musk's view that Optimus is Tesla's largest long-term value driver.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: If the humanoid TAM proves real, Optimus could eventually overtake robotaxi as the main valuation driver beyond 2031.
insights.quote: Humanoid robots could scale to a ~$26 trillion total addressable market, roughly twice that of the robotaxis’ $10-15 trillion.

insights.claim: ARK's model now has external Optimus humanoid sales scaling to ~1 million units and ~$200 billion in Robot-as-a-Service revenue in 2031, versus its 2024 model which assumed only ~30,000 internal humanoids saving ~$3.5 billion in costs in 2029.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A shift from internal cost savings to external revenue is the biggest change in the model and the main reason robotaxi's EV share falls.
insights.quote: external humanoid robot sales scale to ~1 million and generate ~$200 billion in RaaS revenues in 2031

insights.claim: ARK's ~1 million unit Optimus forecast for 2031 is far more conservative than Elon Musk's guidance of 100 million to one billion units in 2031.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Even a bullish house haircuts management's robot guidance by 100-1,000x; Musk's numbers should not be taken at face value.
insights.quote: ARK’s forecast is much more conservative than Elon’s guidance of 100 million to one billion Optimus units in 2031

insights.claim: Informed partly by Tesla's slower-than-expected robotaxi progress, ARK expects Optimus to reach human-level proficiency only around 2031.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: ARK is explicitly using robotaxi delays as a base rate for humanoid timelines, implying meaningful Optimus revenue is back-end loaded.
insights.quote: Informed partly by the slower-than-expected rate of Tesla’s robotaxi progress, Optimus robots could reach human-level proficiency by ~2031

insights.claim: Real-world training data is the humanoid industry's primary bottleneck, and it is harder to collect for Optimus than for robotaxis because humanoids have limited utility when manually operated and won't sell before meeting technical milestones.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Unlike cars, humanoids lack a pre-autonomy sales flywheel for data; firms with captive deployment environments gain an edge.
insights.quote: Today, the industry’s primary bottleneck is real-world training data.

insights.claim: Tesla has launched Optimus Academy to train 20,000 to 30,000 robots internally, and its vertically integrated vehicle factories give it a real-world training and testing advantage over humanoid competitors.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Captive factory environments are a data moat for Tesla in humanoid robotics.
insights.quote: Tesla has launched Optimus Academy to train 20,000 to 30,000 robots internally on various tasks

insights.claim: After manufacturability and safety milestones, ARK expects Optimus capability to scale with compute, reaching human-level proficiency at ~4 GW of compute in 2031.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Ties humanoid progress to a compute/power scaling law, making Tesla a large future buyer of AI chips and power.
insights.quote: Optimus will hit human level proficiency at ~4,000 MW (megawatts) or ~4 GW (gigawatts) of compute in 2031
insights.locator: After reaching manufacturability and safety milestones

insights.claim: ARK's model assumes Tesla scales cumulative AI infrastructure spending from ~$7 billion as of December 2025 to ~$225 billion by end-2031, a new line item that drives Optimus performance.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Implies a massive capex ramp that would make Tesla a major AI-infrastructure spender and a demand source for chip and power suppliers.
insights.quote: scale its spending on AI infrastructure from ~$7 billion cumulatively as of December 2025 to ~$225 billion by the end of 2031

insights.claim: Since 2024, power and compute have become the key differentiators in the AI race, and Elon Musk says chip supply for inference and training will be the long-term constraint, prompting Tesla and SpaceX to launch Terafab jointly.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Vertical integration into chip manufacturing signals Musk companies view foundry capacity as the binding constraint on AI and robotics.
insights.quote: According to Elon, chip supply—for inference and training compute—will be the long-term constraint.

insights.claim: ARK expects SpaceX to fund the larger part of Terafab's yet-to-be-announced capital commitment by building the high-volume terrestrial and orbital manufacturing footprint, while Tesla builds the initial research arm at an estimated cost of $3 billion.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Shifting Terafab's capital burden to SpaceX limits Tesla balance-sheet exposure to a speculative fab buildout.
insights.quote: Tesla focuses on building the initial research arm at an estimated cost of $3 billion

themes.theme: Unmodeled options: Semi, FSD, SpaceX merger

insights.claim: Tesla Semi volume production began at Giga Nevada in September 2026 with an order for ~2,500 trucks, nearly double the entire US Electric Class 8 fleet, yet ARK excludes the Semi from its model.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Semi is free upside to ARK's valuation, though Tesla is prioritizing robotaxi vehicles over trucking.
insights.quote: Tesla has an order for ~2,500 trucks, nearly double the entire Electric Class 8 fleet in the US

insights.claim: ARK estimates autonomous trucking could be a $320 billion addressable market by 2030, but Tesla has signaled it will prioritize high-volume robotaxi vehicles, a market ARK estimates is ~12x larger at scale.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Capital allocation favors robotaxi; investors should not expect trucking to be a material near-term driver.
insights.quote: autonomous trucking could represent a $320 billion addressable market by 2030

insights.claim: FSD reached ~1.5 million active subscriptions as of June 30, 2026, with availability expanding across 8 European countries, but ARK believes most value accrues from the commercial robotaxi service rather than FSD licensing.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: FSD subscriptions are a leading indicator of adoption but not ARK's primary value lever.
insights.quote: At ~1.5 million active subscriptions as of June 30, 2026

insights.claim: ARK says a SpaceX-Tesla merger could happen within five years: Tesla's cash-generative robotaxi network could fund SpaceX's orbital data centers, while SpaceX's frontier AI models could serve as the planning layer for Optimus.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A merger would turn TSLA into a vehicle for SpaceX exposure, with robotaxi cash flows subsidizing space-based compute.
insights.quote: a SpaceX-Tesla merger could take place within the next five years

insights.claim: ARK estimates a combined SpaceX and Tesla could generate $3.8 trillion in revenue and $2.7 trillion in EBIT by 2031, with SpaceX contributing roughly 62% of revenue and 69% of EBIT.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: In ARK's model SpaceX would be the larger economic engine of a combined entity, which matters for merger exchange ratios.

insights.claim: ARK names a slower-than-expected robotaxi ramp as the primary risk to its forecast, caused by regulatory delays or unexpected events such as Elon Musk's sudden departure, a natural disaster, or a pandemic, while arguing regulatory risk is diminishing as robotaxis become safer than human drivers.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Key-person risk and regulation are the swing factors; with ~80% of EV in robotaxi, valuation is highly concentrated on a single execution path.
insights.quote: Now that robotaxis are becoming safer than human-driven cars, regulatory risks seem to be diminishing.
insights.locator: Risks And Limits Of Our Model

insights.claim: ARK's model accounts for full dilution from Elon Musk's stock-based compensation, assuming it vests within the valuation period.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: The per-share target is already net of the Musk pay package, so vesting would not cut into it further.
insights.quote: we also assume that it will vest within the valuation period, a win-win in our view!
